title: The rwb-decision decision-log and rule-catalog contract this QA sample consumes is not in the WP contract-dependency list, and four of its values are named nowhere in the read sources
source: Work Package _work/msr/wp/B2-P4-013.md, story line RWB-P4-E8013-APP (C = [RWB-P3-E1042-CON], I = [], X = [], patterns DP03, DP06, DP13, DP19); _work/msr/context/P4.md (REST operations provided 4: GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session, POST /admin/break-glass-grants; events 0; jobs 1 JOB-18; workflows 0); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E8-013 (Data: decision_log_entry, rule_row, role; Endpoints POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions and .../{versionId}/approve); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.24 (prerequisite FEAT-DRI-03; BR-P4-024; permission checks not given; AC-P4-024-01 'Written one epic ahead'); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T5.2 (calls RuleCatalog and P7 for the decision log), T5.3 (no event), T6.3 (decision-log linkage)
section: RWB-P4-E8013-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 8, 11, 12.2, 12.8 and 14: the population read, the rule-row read, the sample size and tolerance parameter codes, the record code of a sample and of a finding, and the field shape of a member inside inputs_ref
description: The QA sample of RWB-E8-013 reads two things that this service does not own: the closed decisions of a period, which are P7's decision_log_entry, and the rule row of the version each decision was taken under, which is the P7 rule registry. TSD P4 v3 T5.2 names both as calls of the module (RuleCatalog, and P7 for the decision log), so the target story cannot be built without a P7 contract. The Work Package line for RWB-P4-E8013-APP carries C = RWB-P3-E1042-CON only, so the contract story that would publish those two reads is missing from the declared dependency set, and the story builds against that contract and its fake, exactly as the parallel E8007 slice of this epic does. Four further values the story needs are named in no read source: the parameter codes of the sample size and of the tolerance of the control (FSD P4 v3 A2.24.3.1 gives BR-P4-024 and VR-P4-024-1 only, and the TSD gives no parameter row), the record code a QA sample and a QA finding are written under in the local chain of DP-03, the field-level shape of a sample and of a member inside inputs_ref, and the exact P7 paths and query names of the two reads. The story therefore carries the placeholder 'Not specified in the source documents (CG-B2-P4-013-1; ASM-B2-P4-013-1)' for the missing contract and placeholders with ASM-B2-P4-013-2 and ASM-B2-P4-013-3 for the parameter codes and for the record code and field shape, invents no business value, and holds no copy of a decision and no copy of a rule. The legacy endpoints the story inherits (POST /admin/rule-versions and its approve path) are the registry's in the target and are declared as neither provided nor consumed by this gate.
evidence: wp/B2-P4-013.md APP line (C holds one entry, RWB-P3-E1042-CON; patterns hold no DP-04 and no DP-05); context/P4.md service rows (4 provided operations, none of them a decision-log or rule read; 0 events; 0 workflows); FSD P4 v3 A2.24.3.1 (two validation rows and BR-P4-024 only); FSD P4 v3 A2.24.4.1 (AC-P4-024-01 recorded as 'Written one epic ahead', so the criterion carries no values); TSD P4 v3 T5.2 (RuleCatalog and P7 named as calls); TSD P4 v3 T5.3 (event table row 'None'); TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (decision_log_entry.rule_id and rule_version linkage); legacy story RWB-E8-013 (decision_log_entry, rule_row and role in the Data table; the two /admin/rule-versions endpoints); no source names a parameter code for a sample size, a record code for a QA finding or a P7 path
proposed: Add the rwb-decision decision-log and rule-catalog CON story to the contract-dependency list of RWB-P4-E8013-APP (and of RWB-P4-E8013-CON), publish the two reads with their paths and query names, and name the parameter codes of the sample size and of the tolerance with the registry owner and the decision-log owner. Until then, build the two reads against the contract and its fake; at D1 number this row GAP-nnnn and cite it from every placeholder of the two story files and of ASM-B2-P4-013-1 to ASM-B2-P4-013-3.

title: The legacy permission table gives Rules and parameters C and A, but the primary actor of the QA sample holds R only in the role matrix
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E8-013 (Permission checks: Rules and parameters C for RW-COE, A for RW-RISK; Story: 'As a conduct and QA officer'); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T6.1 (RW-CONDUCT Conduct and QA officer: Rules and parameters R, Reference data R, Platform administration '-'; RW-COE: CRUD in Rules and parameters); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.24.3.3 (Conduct and QA officer primary; Center of excellence analyst and Internal audit also use); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md REQ-ACA-003 and REQ-ACA-007
section: RWB-P4-E8013-APP sections 3, 10, 12.1, 16 and 18; RWB-P4-E8013-CON sections 7 (Background), 10, 12.1 and 18
description: The legacy story names the Conduct and QA officer as its actor and lists two permission checks for the feature: Rules and parameters C, held by RW-COE, and Rules and parameters A, held by RW-RISK. The target role matrix of TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-CONDUCT R in Rules and parameters and gives the C letter to RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-PLATADMIN and the other administrative roles; RW-RISK holds RA. A sample drawn and a finding recorded are writes, so the legacy table asks for a C letter the legacy actor does not hold, and the A letter of RW-RISK governs an approval this feature does not perform. The two sources disagree on who runs the control, and neither says which letter the QA panel's write needs in the target. The story resolves it without inventing a matrix value: the write requires Rules and parameters C and the read requires R, as the legacy table and the service's own authorise gate say; the C letter is held by RW-COE today, so RW-COE draws and records until a permission row gives RW-CONDUCT the C letter, which is a data change under FEAT-ACA-04 and not a code change. The A letter of RW-RISK is not used by this gate, because the story approves nothing, and the AC language therefore names C and R only.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E8-013 Permission checks table (Rules and parameters C = RW-COE; A = RW-RISK) against TSD P4 v3 T6.1 row 'RW-CONDUCT Conduct and QA officer | R | R | -' and row 'RW-COE Center of excellence analyst | CRUD | CRUD | R'; FSD P4 v3 A2.24.3.3 (primary actor and the two other roles); FSD P4 v3 A2.24.4.1 (the criterion names no permission); the legacy story's Data and Endpoints tables carry the /admin/rule-versions paths and no QA path
proposed: Confirm with the security administrator which letter the QA panel's write needs in the target. If RW-CONDUCT is to run the control, add or amend the permission row for RULES_AND_PARAMETERS with the letter C in the next matrix version (a data change, no build), and keep the acceptance criteria of both slices on C for the write and R for the read. At D1 number this row GAP-nnnn and cite it from ASM-B2-P4-013-4.

title: The contract baseline fixes two rwb-decision paths, the sample state names and the record field shape that no read source names
source: Work Package _work/msr/wp/B2-P4-013.md (story line RWB-P4-E8013-CON: C = [], patterns DP03, DP06, DP13, DP19); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T-A.1 (no QA, decision-log or rule-catalog path) and T5.2 (RuleCatalog and P7 named as calls only); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.24 (no state and no field list); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md sheet Features (FEAT-ADM-08, one row, no fields); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md R-UNI-38 and R-UNI-39 (no sample state)
section: RWB-P4-E8013-CON sections 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 11, 12.2, 12.8 and 14, and the state set of section 9
description: The contract baseline publishes three operations, four schemas and a sample state set. The three operation paths are fixed by the platform naming rule of DP-13 and by the ownership map of the service, and the field names are taken from the data dictionary. Four elements are not named in any read source: the exact P7 paths and query names of the closed-decision read and the rule-row read, which the document declares as consumed with placeholder paths; the two state names of a sample, which the document fixes as OPEN and COMPLETE because no source names a sample state; the record code a sample and a finding are written under in the DP-03 chain; and the field-level shape of a sample and of a finding inside inputs_ref. The baseline states each of them explicitly, marks the two paths with the placeholder 'Not specified in the source documents (CG-B2-P4-013-3; ASM-B2-P4-013-5)' and the state set and field shape with ASM-B2-P4-013-6, and adds no business value: no sample size, no tolerance, no decision and no rule version is a constant of the document. A path change when the registry contract is published, or a different state name from the audit review, is one line per element and a new version of the document with no change to any schema consumer.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 endpoint inventory (16 rows, none for a QA sample, a decision-log read or a rule-catalog read); TSD P4 v3 T5.2 (RuleCatalog and P7 named as calls, no path); FSD P4 v3 A2.24.4.1 and A2.24.4.3 (no field list, no state, no message for a state); Epics 3 to 8 sheet Features row FEAT-ADM-08 (one sentence); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-38 and R-UNI-39 (rules, no sample state); legacy RWB-E8-013 (no state and no QA path); Work Package CON line (C, I and X empty, so no declared contract to point at)
proposed: Publish the two rwb-decision paths with the registry owner before the wave 4 contract freeze, and confirm the two sample state names with the conduct and QA owner and internal audit. At D1 number this row GAP-nnnn and cite it from ASM-B2-P4-013-5 and ASM-B2-P4-013-6; a path or state change afterwards is a new version v2 of the contract document and no schema change.
